what: Website-fingerprinting resistance of the WireGuard + DAITA carrier, measured with tools/daita_lab.py and tools/wf_attack.py, and protocol identification with nDPI 4.2 (ndpiReader) and TShark 4.4.19

setup.chain: 2 hops in network namespaces (client, relay, exit, destination), constant cells on every hop
setup.latency: netem 10 ms (+-1 ms) at each end of every link: about 60 ms round trip end to end
setup.workload: 8 synthetic sites (main document plus 3-28 objects, 77-594 KB), 15 loads each in shuffled order, 2 parallel connections, sizes +-15% and ~10% of objects skipped per load, 5 s between loads
setup.attack: k-FP-style features plus CUMUL, 500-tree random forest, stratified 5-fold cross-validation; closed world, chance 0.125

views.carrier: client <-> first hop: WireGuard + DAITA, what the client's ISP sees
views.inner link: first hop <-> exit: QUIC with constant cells, no DAITA (the same loads, as a baseline)

windows.true end + 3 s: each load cut at its true end: the attacker is told where every page finished
windows.fixed 6 s: every load gets the same 6 s from its true start: the fairer view of a constant-rate stream

accuracy.reading: Balanced does not stop this attacker. Strong reduces it to the shortest site (S0, whose trace ends inside the window); the other seven are at or near chance, which is Tamaraw's guarantee: only the rounded length of a trace leaks.

strong.rate: one 1380-byte packet every ~21 ms per direction, continuously while keepalives flow

defects found in v0.5.0: FRONT got its padding window as 1-4 microseconds (maybenot-machines takes microseconds; Tamaraw scales seconds itself): every decoy left at once, 1.1 ms apart, at the tunnel's first packet
FRONT ran once per tunnel: no decoys around any later page load, including after WireGuard rekeys

Upstream Tamaraw stopped counting packets once data flowed, so traces were never rounded (5 of 120 a multiple of 100); each ended with ~98 decoys sent 1 us apart, marking when the page finished, and one more decoy after the trace
The QUIC ClientHello between hops named the tool: SNI <role>.advanced-vpn.internal and ALPN advanced-vpn/1, readable by anyone on the path (QUIC Initial packets are decryptable)

protocol identification.carrier: nDPI: WireGuard, category VPN, by DPI. DAITA hides what is sent, not that WireGuard is used.
protocol identification.between hops, v0.5.0: nDPI: QUIC, Hostname/SNI exit.advanced-vpn.internal, ALPN advanced-vpn/1
protocol identification.between hops, now: nDPI: QUIC, category Web, ALPN h3, no hostname

padding.carrier data packets: every WireGuard data packet 1380 bytes on the wire (14,706 balanced, 29,565 strong); only handshakes (156/100) and empty keepalives (40) differ
